questions.q: What is the core question that decides between a UI Policy and a Data Policy?
options: Whether the rule needs to hold true only on the form, or no matter how the record is written
Whether the table involved is Incident or Change Request
Whether the admin prefers writing JavaScript
Whether the organization has more than one ServiceNow instance
questions.explain: That single distinction — form-only vs. every write path — is exactly what separates a UI Policy use case from a Data Policy use case.

questions.q: Hiding an irrelevant field purely to reduce form clutter, with no real consequence if some other write path ignores the rule, is a good example of which mechanism?
options: A Business Rule
A UI Policy
A Data Policy with Apply to UI off
A Scripted REST API
questions.explain: Pure form-UX convenience with no integrity stakes is the textbook case for a UI Policy alone.

questions.q: "Business Justification is mandatory for any Priority-1 Incident, even if created via an API integration" calls for which mechanism?
options: A UI Policy, because it evaluates faster
A Data Policy, because the rule must hold true regardless of the write path
Neither — this cannot be enforced in ServiceNow
A UI Policy with reverse-if-false turned off
questions.explain: Because the requirement must hold true no matter how the record is created, only a Data Policy's server-side enforcement can guarantee it.

questions.q: What practical default do many experienced admins use when deciding between the two?
options: Always use a UI Policy, since Data Policies are deprecated
Always use a Data Policy, since UI Policies no longer work
Default to a Data Policy whenever real data integrity is at stake, and reserve UI Policy for pure form-UX convenience
Use whichever one was used last on that table
questions.explain: This default holds up because a Data Policy can still mirror its behavior onto the form via Apply to UI, so little is lost by defaulting to it when integrity matters.

questions.q: Why can't a Data Policy alone handle a requirement to hide a field based on a condition?
options: Data Policies can control visibility, but only when Apply to UI is off
Data Policies never control Visible/hidden behavior at all — only mandatory and read-only
Data Policies can only apply to the Incident table
Hiding fields requires a Business Rule, not either policy type
questions.explain: Visible/hidden is a UI-only effect; Data Policies are limited to mandatory and read-only, so hiding a field always requires an actual UI Policy.
